channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Copper: AI-driven demand reshapes pricing – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Commodity Compass Analytics team, led by Michael Haigh and Jeremy Sellem, argues that Copper has been increasingly driven by AI-related demand, arbitrage flows and US trade policy since February 2025.

item.title: Japanese Yen slips as US Dollar stabilizes, US PCE in focus
item.description: USD/JPY edges higher on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) finds some stability following last week’s sharp volatility, with geopolitical developments back in focus as the United States prepares to widen secondary sanctions against Iran.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade shock weighs against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note that the Canadian Dollar (CAD) is the main G10 underperformer after US/Canada trade talks collapsed. Ottawa’s pledge to respond to tariffs and provide domestic aid raises uncertainty for Canadian businesses.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Jackson Hole communication focus – Wells Fargo
item.description: Wells Fargo Economics argues that Jackson Hole is often overhyped, with only a couple of truly consequential speeches in the past 14 years.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Rates seen on hold then higher – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities expects the Bank of Canada to maintain the Overnight Rate at 2.25% through 2026, despite headline CPI near the top of its target range.

item.title: US President Trump announces tariffs on Canadian autos, trucks and steel
item.description: United States (US) President Donald Trump has announced a sharp escalation in the trade fight with Canada, declaring that beginning January 1, 2027, the United States will raise tariffs to 50% on all cars, trucks, automotive parts, and steel imported from its northern neighbor.

item.title: US Dollar: Weakness may stabilize as US growth advantage persists - BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes that the Treasury’s buyback announcement initially pushed longer-term Treasuries lower, weakened the Dollar and boosted Gold. He argues the USD slump should stabilize this week, with the US growth advantage offsetting fiscal concerns.

item.title: Canadian Dollar slides as Trump escalates trade war with Canada
item.description: USD/CAD extends its advance on Monday, trading around 1.3830 at the time of writing, up 0.52% on the day.

item.title: Euro: Rally vulnerable to reversal against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret highlight that the Euro (EUR) is softer against the Dollar (USD) after an almost 3% rally from late July, with price action turning defensive.

item.title: Gold extends gains as US Treasury buyback fallout keeps buyers in control
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD)extends its intraday advance on Monday, building on the strong rally seen last week following the US Treasury’s buyback announcement. At the time of writing, XAU/USD trades around $4,674, up nearly 1.5% on the day at levels last seen on May 14.

item.title: Canada: Tariffs reshape outlook – RBC
item.description: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC) analyzes new Section 338 U.S. tariffs on Canadian exports, noting a 50% rate on goods representing about 5% of Canada’s exports to the United States.

item.title: Euro holds ground as US Dollar steadies, markets brace for Iran sanctions
item.description: EUR/USD trades flat on Monday as the US Dollar (USD) steadies and markets settle into a calmer tone following the sharp volatility triggered by the US Treasury’s surprise buyback announcement last week. At the time of writing, the pair trades around 1.1670, hovering near levels last seen in mid-May.

item.title: Federal Reserve: Warsh faces a communication test – DBS
item.description: DBS Bank strategist Philip Wee argues that Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh’s rejection of forward guidance is amplifying market volatility and complicating the policy mix with the Treasury.

item.title: Reuters: US Treasury's Scott Bessent to announce more sanctions on Iran
item.description: The United States (US) Treasury is expected to broaden the scope of secondary sanctions it can impose on entities and countries that maintain business ties with Iran, reports Reuters.

item.title: United States: Sideways growth with stagflation risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategists expect United States (US) output growth to move sideways in 2026, with their Gross Domestic Product (GDP) tracker at 2.5% quarter-on-quarter annualized and full-year growth slightly below trend at 2.1% Q4/Q4.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Trade war escalation threatens recent strength – MUFG
item.description: MUFG's Derek Halpenny argues the Canadian Dollar’s (CAD) reaction to the new US tariffs on USD 20bn of Canadian exports will hinge on escalation risks rather than the initial measures.

item.title: Euro: Range consolidation against US Dollar as growth gap narrows – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kit Juckes notes EUR/USD has retraced half of its drop from above 1.20 to 1.1325 and is now stuck in a range as markets await fresh US data.

item.title: US Dollar: Policy risks keep downside bias – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner, Francesco Pesole and Frantisek Taborsky note the Dollar starts the week soft as markets await US policy signals from the White House.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Cooling inflation but carry remains supportive – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad expects Australia’s July Consumer Price Index (CPI) to ease, with headline and trimmed mean inflation drifting lower, in line with softer labor conditions and wage growth.

item.title: WTI Oil retreats toward $85 ahead of US economic offensive against Iran
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil falls 1.55% on Monday and trades around $85.00 at the time of writing, giving back some of its recent gains as investors take profits ahead of the announcement of new US sanctions against Iran.

item.title: CEE FX: Koruna leads as policy diverges – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reviews recent CEE FX performance, noting that the euro’s strength above 1.17 has supported high-beta PLN and HUF, while the Czech koruna has also gained despite its lower beta profile.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Buyers stall near $70 after strong rally
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) is little changed on Monday, fluctuating between modest gains and losses near its highest level since mid-June, with buyers struggling to clear the $70 psychological mark.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: MNB easing and HUF carry prospects – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu describes Hungary as a constructive story within EMEA, with post-election re-rating and scope for continued MNB easing.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: GDP rebound supports Loonie – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities economists Robert Both and Emma Lawrence expect Canada’s Q2 National Accounts to show a sharp rebound in Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth, driven by stronger exports and solid services activity.

item.title: US Dollar: Debasement narrative caps upside – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note that the US Treasury’s expanded long-end buyback programme has revived market fears of Dollar debasement, driving a weaker USD, stronger Gold and higher breakevens.

item.title: Experts agree: Japanese Yen needs more than intervention to take off from lows
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) extends losses against the US Dollar (USD) in a calm trading session on Monday.

item.title: Gold: Breakout sustains upward momentum – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts highlight that Gold has broken out of a small base formation, reclaimed its 200‑DMA and is enjoying an extended rebound. The move is framed within broader Dollar debasement concerns and rising term premium.

item.title: Euro: Positioning supports gradual gains against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights futures data showing asset managers and leveraged funds adding Euro exposure, leaving speculators underweight. He notes recovering German IFO and Eurozone PMIs, and sees limited need for EUR/USD to drop sharply below 1.1660/70 unless risk assets suffer.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Retail slump yet hikes priced – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad highlights that New Zealand retail sales volumes unexpectedly fell in Q2, driven by fuel and motor-related categories, while core sales still rose, showing resilient domestic demand.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Aussie eases from 12-week highs with bulls still in command
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) ticks lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, but maintains its broader bullish tone, with the AUD/USD pair trading at 0.7164, a few pips shy of the 12-week high of 0.7180 hit last Friday.
